title: Evaluate ONNX Embedding Models for Hybrid Semantic Search
description:
Problem: MemorySmith already supports one local ONNX embedding provider for semantic and hybrid search, but the current implementation is tuned around a narrow E5-style contract: one configured model path, one vocabulary path, WordPiece tokenization, `query:`/`passage:` prefixes, and dense single-vector output. That is workable for the current wiki and memory corpus, but it leaves an unresolved product decision: should MemorySmith keep E5 as the default, switch to a longer-context model, or add a pluggable provider seam so deployments can choose the model that best fits their local LLM resource budget and retrieval goals?

Evidence from the 2026-05-25 review:
- `MemorySmith.App/Services/MemorySmithOptions.cs` exposes a single `SemanticSearch.ModelPath` and `VocabularyPath`, not a model-family abstraction.
- `MemorySmith.App/Services/SemanticEmbeddingSearchService.cs` currently assumes dense embeddings, E5-style query/document prefix handling, and a WordPiece vocabulary-backed tokenizer.
- `MemorySmith.Tests/ModelBackedSearchBenchmarkTests.cs` already provides MemorySmith-specific semantic, hybrid, and throughput guardrails for model-backed search.
- `Data/Models` currently contains local assets for the active embedding path plus candidate ONNX files: `e5-base-v2.onnx`, `nomic-embed-text-v1.5.onnx`, `jjina-embeddings-v2-base-code_model_fp16.onnx`, `embedding-model.onnx`, and one `vocab.txt`.
- Internet research suggests longer-context models such as Nomic and Jina may help technical or code-heavy retrieval, but those claims need MemorySmith-specific validation because this product already uses Lucene BM25 plus RRF and co-hosts a local LLM.

Desired outcome: produce an evidence-backed recommendation for MemorySmith's local semantic-search stack: stay on the current E5-family baseline, adopt one of the staged alternatives, or add a model-agnostic provider seam first and defer any default-model switch until compatibility work is complete.

Scope:
- In scope: evaluate at minimum the current E5 baseline plus the locally staged Nomic and Jina candidates under `Data/Models`.
- In scope: compare relevance, hybrid rank behavior, warm-path latency, throughput, memory/footprint, context-window implications, and practical support burden for a local LLM plus Lucene BM25/RRF deployment.
- In scope: verify tokenizer, pooling, prefix, vocabulary, and output-dimension compatibility with the current C# ONNX provider; explicitly call out when a candidate is not drop-in.
- In scope: recommend whether MemorySmith should keep one default model, expose a configuration-driven provider strategy, or create a follow-up implementation task before any model switch.
- Out of scope: adding ANN/vector-database infrastructure, broad AST-based repo chunking, or adopting multi-vector BGE-M3 style retrieval in the same task. Lucene already provides the sparse leg today, so multi-vector dense-plus-sparse experiments belong in a separate follow-up if still desired.

Acceptance criteria:
- A side-by-side comparison exists for the current E5 path, Nomic, and Jina using the same MemorySmith corpus and local hardware profile.
- The comparison covers context window, on-disk footprint, tokenizer/runtime compatibility, query/document formatting requirements, output dimensionality, relevance results, latency results, and local-LLM resource tradeoffs.
- The task ends with an explicit recommendation: keep E5, change the default model, or add model-provider abstraction first.
- If a non-drop-in candidate clearly wins, a follow-up task exists that scopes the required provider/tokenizer/pooling/configuration work before adoption.

Validation:
- Run `MemorySmith.Tests/ModelBackedSearchBenchmarkTests.cs` or equivalent focused model-backed benchmark slices for each viable candidate.
- Add focused provider tests if a candidate requires different tokenization, pooling, or prompt formatting behavior.
- Run `Scripts/Test-TaskRecords.ps1` after task metadata changes.

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Rewritten during task review to separate model evaluation from provider abstraction. Current search already has model-backed relevance and latency guards plus a single-provider ONNX seam, so this task should prove whether E5 remains the right default for MemorySmith's Lucene + RRF + local-LLM stack instead of assuming a generic internet ranking applies unchanged.

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Priority lowered to Low while near-term search work focuses on modular provider seams, cache correctness, and regression coverage. Treat this as a follow-on evaluation task after the current provider becomes easier to transition safely.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body: 2026-08-08 deep-dive found ordinary semantic benchmark cases exercise token fallback when no SemanticEmbeddingSearchService is injected, while model-backed cases Assert.Ignore when ONNX is unavailable. Keep real-provider metadata and deterministic fallback coverage explicitly separate; TSK-0466 tracks the wiring gap.
